  • Decisions (ADRs)
    • 0001 — The docs site is public, with a publication boundary
    • 0002 — Mirror the access logs unfiltered; interpret with views
    • 0003 — Request logging after the Cloudflare cutover
    • 0004 — Download statistics are generated static files, not a live service
    • 0005 — Completeness is measured by origin, not by page type
    • 0006 — 33 of 35 releases, and checkResults for them, are archival
    • 0007 — Cloudflare Workflows carries the human-approval gate, starting with the release roll
    • 0008 — Split by audience into three repositories; migrate by strangling behind the Worker
    • 0009 — Client addresses are hashed at the edge, not de-identified downstream
    • 0010 — Two new repos for the parallel build system; the governance file is the manifest, not a registry
    • 0011 — One propagation gate for every producer
    • 0012 — Client addresses are stored raw; de-identification is a view
    • 0013 — A redirect lands on the content, or it goes

Roadmap

Modified

September 30, 2026

Four milestones, in dependency order. Each has an umbrella tracking issue in this repo where progress is checked off; implementation issues are filed in the repo where the work happens (where to file issues) and linked from the umbrella’s checklist. This page is the narrative; the issues are the ledger. When they disagree, fix whichever is wrong.

M0 — Operational readiness (#1)

The floor the rest stands on: every repo public, consistently named, licensed, contributable, tested, and watched. Mostly done 2026-08-21.

Acceptance criteria

Dependencies: none.

M1 — Production cutover (#2)

Done: bioconductor.org has been served by the new edge since 2026-09-28 (nameservers to Cloudflare at 17:30 UTC, the site at about 20:09 UTC; runbook and log). What remains is closing out the flip: the week of monitoring ends 2026-10-05, and Route53 stays the rollback target, with a record freeze, until 2026-10-12. How the system works now is on How bioconductor.org works; who runs it and the rollback steps are on Operations.

Several pre-flip gates were overtaken by the flip itself. They are restated below as what the running system has to show, with what replaced each.

Acceptance criteria

Checkboxes here mirror #2.

Tasks

Dependencies: M0 — the daily checks are what watches the flip.

M2 — Full disconnect from legacy infrastructure (#3)

The new stack serves production but still depends on master: packages arrive by the hourly sync from master’s docroot. (The /packages/stats/ tree no longer does: it is generated by bioc-traffic and served from R2.) M2 ends the dependency: master, staging, the legacy build system, and the legacy stats pipeline all retire, and roughly $5,000/month of AWS with them. Parity with master (bioc-edge #43-#48) has to be clean before master goes.

Acceptance criteria

Tasks

Dependencies: M1, done except for the parity fixes, which M2 needs too.

M3 — Search and page redesigns, through the public PR process (#4)

Two goals in one: a real search story, and visible redesign work used deliberately to prove the contribution loop — PR → preview URL → review → merge → route flip.

Acceptance criteria

Tasks

Dependencies: none left; M1 put the Astro build in production.
